failure_modes: Pooling kinematics across behavioural regimes blurs regime-specific motion that is itself a product of coordination
Unmodelled environmental drivers (pheromone fields, food, boundaries) let the null miss structure that is not social
Too few realisations to estimate the null distribution of the measure
gloss: Simulate agents that move like the real ones but ignore each other, to test for social structure
invariants: Each synthetic agent moves independently of every other agent
Marginal speed distribution, speed autocorrelation, speed-dependent turning and entry/exit timeline match the data
Synthetic trajectories pass through the identical interaction and network pipeline
mechanism: A {{null_model_baseline}} for trajectory data that keeps individual kinematics and removes coordination. From pooled tracking data estimate: (1) a two-state stationary/moving Markov chain, with an agent stationary when speed < v_min (1 px/frame) and persistence P_SS = N_SS/(N_SS+N_SM), P_SM = N_MM/(N_MM+N_MS); (2) a first-order speed-transition matrix over N_v = 30 speed bins with Laplace smoothing, P[m,n] = (T_mn + eps)/sum_l(T_ml + eps), eps = 0.01; (3) speed-conditioned turning angles, dtheta | v_i ~ N(mu_i, sigma_i^2), so slow agents turn more; (4) entry statistics (x0, y0, v0, theta0) from first appearances. Simulate agents independently: spawn at edges to match the empirical head-count timeline N_a(t), remove those that exit, switch motion state with probabilities 1-P_SS and 1-P_SM, update speed with momentum v_{t+1} = zeta v_t + (1-zeta) v_sampled (zeta = 0.6), give stationary agents U(0, 0.3) px/frame jitter to mimic tracking noise, wrap heading to [-pi, pi], and step x += v cos(theta), y += v sin(theta). Run many realisations (25 per experiment) through the same network construction. Differences that remain are evidence of interaction rules, memory or task allocation rather than motion statistics.
preconditions: Tracked trajectories with stable identities and a speed cutoff that removes non-physical jumps (e.g. 120 px/frame)
